title: Storage Retention Catalog
description: Single source of truth for storage retention (AL-01). Each entry declares, for one repo-relative directory, what class of artifact lives there, how long it is retained (ttl_days), and what happens on expiry (action). Consumed by libs/core/storage-retention-catalog.ts, which falls back to built-in defaults mirroring the pre-catalog constants when this file is missing or invalid — the janitor never dies because of a bad catalog. Entries without ttl_days are note-only declarations (e.g. self-expiring stores); directories with no entry at all are never deleted and, under active/shared/runtime/, are surfaced by the janitor report as uncovered.

version.description: Semver of this catalog format. Bump minor for additive vocabulary, major for a change to enforcement semantics.

description.description: Free-text human note describing the intent of this catalog.

entries.description: Retention declarations. Paths must be unique (enforced by the loader).

path.description: Repo-relative directory governed by this rule (POSIX separators, no leading/trailing slash, no '..').

artifact_class.description: What kind of artifact the directory holds. evidence = execution/audit evidence; report = generated reports; export = outbound deliverables; cache = regenerable intermediates; tmp = consumable scratch; log = append-only logs; state = load-bearing runtime state (registries, locks, sessions, tokens) — never TTL-deleted, pair with action review_required (AL-04).

ttl_days.description: Retention period in days, evaluated against file mtime. Omit for note-only entries whose contents self-expire (the note must explain the mechanism).

action.description: What the janitor does when the entry's condition is met. delete = remove the expired file; archive = move the expired file to active/archive/<repo-relative-path> (implemented; never auto-deleted afterwards); review_required = no automatic deletion ever — the directory is declared (never reported uncovered) and surfaced in the janitor report for a human retention decision (AL-04); rotate = file-level action for append-only .jsonl ledgers — rename the live file to a <name>-<YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>.jsonl segment once it exceeds rotate_min_bytes, then expire segments by ttl_days via segment_action; compact = file-level action for versioned keyed .jsonl stores — fold to the last record per compact_key once the file exceeds compact_min_bytes and archive the pre-compaction file.

rotate_min_bytes.description: rotate action: live-file size in bytes that triggers rotation (default 8 MiB).

segment_action.description: rotate action: how expired rotated segments are disposed. Default delete; archive moves segments under active/archive/ for evidence-class ledgers.

compact_key.description: compact action: record field identifying the keyed entity (e.g. item_id). Required for action=compact.

self_managed.description: rotate / compact action: the writer owns live-file retention (it maintains the file inline under its own lock, e.g. a dedupe window that must survive). The janitor never rotates or compacts the live file; it only expires already-rotated segments by ttl_days via segment_action.

compact_min_bytes.description: compact action: live-file size in bytes that triggers compaction (default 4 MiB).

audit.description: When true, expiry actions must leave an audit record (active/shared/logs/audit/storage-retention.jsonl).

soft_delete_days.description: AL-04 soft-delete grace: expired files are moved to active/archive/.trash/<original-repo-relative-path> instead of unlinked, and purged from the trash only after this many further days (mtime-based). Omit for immediate hard delete.

code_grace_days.description: Scratch promotion grace (active/shared/tmp only): an unpromoted job directory holding authored code (*.ts, *.mts, *.js, *.mjs, *.py, *.sh) or an ADF JSON (top-level steps array) keeps its files this many days beyond ttl_days; while the grace runs the janitor warns with the exact pnpm scratch:promote command and lists the directory in active/shared/runtime/system/scratch-promotion-candidates.json. A TOOL.json or .scratch-promoted.json in the job directory counts as promoted. Default 2 when omitted.

backup.description: Backup opt-out (scripts/lib/backup-file-selection.ts). exclude = `--scope all|mission|tenant` backups leave this directory out because it is fully regenerable (rebuildable index, provider/probe cache, test-run fixtures, daemon sockets). Omit for everything else: a cache/tmp class alone never excludes, since staging stores (distill or promotion candidates, queued events, mailboxes) hold pending state a restore needs. The tmp/staging/cache floor roots are always excluded.

note.description: Human rationale: why this TTL/action, and any special expiry mechanism.

status_rules.description: WI-16: per-file status-aware expiry rules nested under this directory. Each rule reads one JSON status field and one JSON date field out of every file its path_pattern matches, instead of trusting directory mtime — closing the gap where a directory-level TTL cannot distinguish a stale pending_review file from a confirmed one in the same tree.

id.description: Stable identifier, recorded in the janitor's deletion audit line.

path_pattern.description: Glob-like path relative to the owning entry's directory (no leading/trailing slash, no '..', no absolute path). '*' matches within one path segment only, never across '/'. Example: "*/work-inventory/observations/*.json".

status_field.description: Top-level JSON field read from each matched file and tested against "statuses".

statuses.description: The file is a candidate only when status_field's value is one of these.

age_field.description: Top-level JSON field (ISO date string) the ttl_days is measured from.

ttl_days.description: Retention period in days, evaluated against age_field's value.

action.description: Only delete is implemented: the matched file is expired through the same audited expireFilePerPolicy path a directory-level delete entry uses (soft-delete when the owning entry declares soft_delete_days).
